title: Snap-through of a shallow arch by arc length
source: One-mode closed form of a shallow sinusoidal arch y₀ = a sin(πx/L) on pins at a fixed span under q₀ sin(πx/L): q₀ = EI k⁴ [c + (a − c)(2ac − c²)/(4r²)], k = π/L, limit points at c = a ∓ r √((a²/r² − 4)/3) (S. P. Timoshenko, J. M. Gere, Theory of Elastic Stability, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill 1961, §7.6; Y. C. Fung, A. Kaplan, NACA TN 2840, 1952): L = 100, h = 1, unit width, E = 10⁴, ν = 0, a/r = 3.5; the load is scaled to the upper limit load, so the peak load factor is 1 and the valley 0.211035

quantities.reason: 40 × 2 × 1 hex20 against shallow Euler–Bernoulli arch theory, the load piecewise constant per element, and the limit load picked from converged states (second order in the arc)
as the peak; the valley is a fifth of the peak load and a small difference of the bending and axial terms, so its tolerance is stated as 2 % of the peak load

quantities.quantity: negative eigenvalues of the tangent past the upper limit point
quantities.reason: the inertia of the LDLᵀ factor: exactly one unstable direction between the limit points
